rationale: Round 0 built and ran correctly with no ICE, so this round raises obfuscation pressure while staying bounded: md5.c is tiny (317 lines, 7 functions) with md5_process as the single hot, arithmetic-dense function (3076/4819 text bytes), so SUB gets the highest weights on every dimension — boolean/arithmetic substitution is nearly free at runtime, lands squarely on the bit-manipulation-heavy features of MD5, and carries negligible correctness risk given a clean prior build. FLA is the second-strongest lever because md5_process and main have multi-branch loop structure that flattening obfuscates well, but its RuntimeCost weight is held to 0.50 to protect the hot loop, and SPLIT is boosted (high cost tolerances, low risk) to enlarge basic blocks so FLA/BCF have more material to restructure. BCF is raised moderately for layered bogus-path resistance but with the lowest cost tolerances of the control-flow passes since it inflates both cycles and size on a program whose entire binary is under 5 KB — size growth must stay proportionate. IBR and ICALL get modest mid-range weights: this codebase has few indirectible branches and calls (md5_update/md5_finish call sites only), so their marginal security gain doesn't justify aggressive application, and their CorrectnessRisk tolerances stay lowest to avoid destabilizing the few call sites that carry the benchmark's observable output. IGV stays enabled at low gain weights since md5.c has minimal global state, making it a cheap diversity add-on with little downside.
